title: The Role of HIF-1alpha/BNIP3 Pathway in Hippocampal Neuronal Autophagy in Epilepsy.
authors: Kuang, Huimin; Meng, Youshi; Qin, Xinran; Qian, Kai; Gong, Chi; Li, Sijun; Zhang, Lin; Gan, Xiaohang; Lu, Yuling; Wu, Yuan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究癫痫中海马神经元自噬的HIF-1alpha/BNIP3通路，仅涉及基因表达与机器学习诊断，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Epilepsy (EP), a prevalent neurological disorder, lacks a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying epileptogenesis. Multiple studies highlight that hippocampal (Hip) neuronal injury may serve as an essential underlying factor in EP onset and progression. Accumulating evidence shows that autophagy (Apg) has an essential function in supporting cell survival and sustaining cellular and tissue homeostasis. This investigation aimed to examine and further validate hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1alpha/BNIP3 signaling in the Hip neuronal Apg in a lithium chloride-pilocarpine (LiCl-Pilo)-induced EP rat model. We retrieved the GSE143272 dataset and generally validated Apg-related genes (ATGs) expression and its diagnostic roles in EP through differential expression analysis, protein-protein interaction (PPI), enrichment analysis, and four machine learning (ML) models. Afterward, the predictive performance of the ML models was evaluated via a nomogram model and validated with an external dataset (GSE63808). Finally, the function of the HIF-1alpha/BNIP3 pathway in regulating Apg through HIF-1alpha inhibition was systematically validated in the LiCl-Pilo-induced chronic EP rat model. Our data identified eleven ATGs as differentially expressed. Among them, HIF-1alpha and BNIP3 were found to be closely associated, exhibiting a negative regulatory interaction. The ML model XGB exhibited superior performance in differentiating EP patients. Subsequent experimental validation confirmed elevated Apg markers and HIF-1alpha levels, along with decreased BNIP3 levels. Inhibition of HIF-1alpha upregulated HIF-1alpha/BNIP3-modulated Apg and attenuated Hip neuron damage and mitochondrial damage induced by LiCl-Pilo-induced EP. Collectively, these outcomes suggest that HIF-1alpha/BNIP3 signaling might be involved in neuronal damage by mediating Hip Apg, thereby regulating epileptic seizures.
abstract_zh: 癫痫（EP）作为一种常见的神经系统疾病，其癫痫发生（epileptogenesis）的分子机制尚未得到全面理解。多项研究强调，海马（Hip）神经元损伤可能是EP发生和进展的关键潜在因素。越来越多的证据表明，自噬（Apg）在支持细胞存活及维持细胞和组织稳态中发挥重要作用。本研究旨在探讨并进一步验证在氯化锂-毛果芸香碱（LiCl-Pilo）诱导的EP大鼠模型中，缺氧诱导因子（HIF）-1α/BNIP3信号通路在海马神经元自噬中的作用。我们获取了GSE143272数据集，并通过差异表达分析、蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）、富集分析及四种机器学习（ML）模型，普遍验证了自噬相关基因（ATGs）的表达及其在EP中的诊断作用。随后，通过列线图模型评估了ML模型的预测性能，并使用外部数据集（GSE63808）进行验证。最后，在LiCl-Pilo诱导的慢性EP大鼠模型中，通过抑制HIF-1α系统验证了HIF-1α/BNIP3通路在调控自噬中的功能。我们的数据识别出11个差异表达的ATGs。其中，HIF-1α和BNIP3被发现密切相关，并表现出负调控相互作用。ML模型XGB在区分EP患者方面表现出优越性能。后续实验验证证实，自噬标志物和HIF-1α水平升高，而BNIP3水平降低。抑制HIF-1α上调了HIF-1α/BNIP3调控的自噬，并减轻了LiCl-Pilo诱导的EP引起的海马神经元损伤和线粒体损伤。综合来看，这些结果表明HIF-1α/BNIP3信号可能通过介导海马自噬参与神经元损伤，从而调节癫痫发作。
